title: The US Army Looks to the Pacific – and Space – for Future Relevance
author: Robert Farley
text:
Soldiers assigned to the 7th Infantry Division (Multi-Domain Command – Pacific) conduct unmanned aerial systems tests during exercise Bayonet Quest 2026 in Alpena, Michigan, Oct. 5, 2026.
Credit: U.S. Army video by Sgt. Pomare Te’o Jr.
The U.S. Army sees its future as preparing for a fight in the Pacific, and it’s taking lessons from both the current fight in the Middle East and Russia’s ongoing war with Ukraine. In addition to missiles, drones, and electronic warfare, that means an increasing presence for the land service in the space domain. The effort represents an attempt by the Army to maintain its relevance under geographical constraints that are less than ideal, and in an institutional context that increasingly favors long-range, high-end unmanned systems. Both the U.S. Navy and the U.S. Air Force have experienced embarrassing setbacks in the present war against Iran, the former because of an overcommitment of its aircraft carrier fleet and the latter because of the loss of several key assets in combat. Nevertheless, both services have contributed immensely to ongoing operations. The contribution of the U.S. Army has been more limited and less visible, in large part because of the reluctance of the Trump administration to develop serious plans for an invasion of Iran. [...]
